==English== {{wp|}} ===Etymology=== {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:title>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|title}}, {{m|enm|titel}}, from {{inh|en|ang|titul||title, heading, superscription}}, from {{der|en|la|titulus||title, inscription}}. {{doublet|en|tilde|[[titer]]/[[titre]]|titlo|tittle|titulus}}. ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/ˈtaɪ̯.təl/|[ˈtʰaɪ̯.tʰəl]|~|[ˈtʰaɪ̯.tʰl̩]}} * {{IPA|en|/ˈtaɪ̯.ɾəl/|[ˈtʰaɪ̯.ɾəl]|~|[ˈtʰaɪ̯.ɾl̩]|aa=t-flapping}} ** {{audio|en|en-us-title.ogg|a=US}} * {{rhymes|en|aɪtəl|s=2}} * {{hyph|en|ti|tle}} * {{hmp|en|tidal|aa1=t-flapping}} ===Noun=== {{en-noun}} # The [[name]] of a film, musical piece, [[painting]], or other [[work of art]]. #: {{ux|en|I know the singer's name, but not the '''title''' of the song.}} # The name of a writing such as a book, which identifies it and usually describes its [[subject]], with a short [[phrase]] that often [[summarize]]s its topic. # {{lb|en|by extension}} A [[publish]]ed piece of [[media]]. #: {{ux|en|The retailer carries thousands of '''titles'''.}} #: {{ux|en|Buyers of the new video game console can choose from three bundled '''titles'''.}} # {{lb|en|by extension}} A section or division of a writing, as of an [[act]] of [[law]] or a book. #: {{ux|en|'''Title''' II of the USA PATRIOT Act}} # {{senseid|en|appellation for rank, job, qualification, etc}} An [[appellation]] given to a person or [[family]] to signify either [[veneration]], official [[position]], [[social]] [[rank]], the [[possession]] of [[asset]]s or [[property|properties]], or a professional or academic [[qualification]], such as {{m|en|Mister}}, {{m|en|Mr}}, {{m|en|Ms}}, {{m|en|Doctor}}, or {{m|en|Dr}}; {{ng|for more examples, see [[:Category:en:Titles]]}}. #: {{syn|en|style}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Macbeth|act=I|scene=ii|passage=Our bosom interest: go pronounce his present death
With his former '''title''' greet Macbeth.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1913|author={{w|Edgar Rice Burroughs}}|title={{w|The Return of Tarzan}}|publisher=Ballantine Books|location=New York|year_published=1963|page=100|passage=The old man had always favored the match. He liked Clayton, and, being of an old southern family, he put rather an exaggerated value on the advantages of a '''title''', which meant little or nothing to his daughter.}} #* {{RQ:Travers Cuckoo in the Nest|chapter=1|passage=He read the letter aloud. Sophia listened with the studied air of one for whom, even in these days, a '''title''' possessed some surreptitious allurement.}} # {{senseid|en|ownership}} {{lb|en|property law}} Legal right to ownership of a property; a [[deed]] or other [[certificate]] proving this. #: {{ux|en|a good '''title''' to an estate, or an imperfect '''title'''}} # In canon law, that by which a [[beneficiary]] holds a [[benefice]]. # A [[church]] to which a [[priest]] was [[ordain]]ed, and where he was to [[reside]]. # {{lb|en|mostly|in the plural}} A written title, [[credit]], or [[caption]] shown with a film, video, or performance. #: {{ux|en|The '''titles''' scrolled by too quickly to read.}} # {{lb|en|sports}} The recognition given to the [[winner]] of a [[championship]] in sports. # {{lb|en|bookbinding}} The panel for the name, between the bands of the back of a book. #* {{quote-journal|en|date=May 13, 2012|author=Phil McNulty|work=BBC Sport |title=[http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/17973148 Man City 3-2 QPR] |passage=With some City fans already leaving the stadium in tears, Edin Dzeko equalised in the second of five minutes of stoppage time before Sergio Aguero scored the goal that won the '''title'''.}} # {{lb|en|law|formal}} A [[long title]]. # {{lb|en|law|informal}} A [[short title]]. ====Synonyms==== * See also
